statement: message = array of [Type, Data?] tuples; one array passed to ctx.down/ctx.up = one wave; in-process representation = tuple, wire representation = protobuf, decoupled at the wire-bridge boundary
rationale: D8 up/down(msgs); D11 tuple/protobuf decoupled

statement: 10 message types, CLOSED: START + DIRTY/DATA/RESOLVED/INVALIDATE/COMPLETE/ERROR/TEARDOWN/PAUSE/RESUME. No open set, no user-defined custom types, no MessageTypeRegistry; the old unknown-type-forwarding rule is retired (vacuous under a closed set). Adding a tier/type = spec change (constitutional)
rationale: D9 9-type closed set + START handshake; D18 messageTier compile-time const, custom types CUT

statement: messageTier const table (7 tiers): 0 START(handshake) / 1 PAUSE·RESUME(control) / 2 DIRTY(notification) / 3 DATA·RESOLVED(value) / 4 INVALIDATE(settle) / 5 COMPLETE·ERROR(terminal) / 6 TEARDOWN. Tiers <3 dispatch immediately; tiers ≥3 are batch-deferred (DATA/RESOLVED in the settle slice, INVALIDATE alongside, terminal after, TEARDOWN last). Closed const table — adding a tier is constitutional
rationale: D34 ratified numbering (old-spec with PAUSE/RESUME↔DIRTY swap so control precedes notification); D9 closed set

statement: [DATA,v] requires a non-SENTINEL payload (v ≠ undefined/None/per-language sentinel); [ERROR,e] requires a non-SENTINEL payload; bare [DATA]/[ERROR] and [DATA,SENTINEL] are rejected at the dispatch boundary; null is a valid DATA value (domain-level absence)
rationale: D16 SENTINEL = absence-of-DATA must stay decidable; DATA(SENTINEL) would be indistinguishable from never-emitted

statement: outside batch: one ctx.down(msgs) = one wave; inside batch: accumulation until commit = one wave

every tier-3 (DATA/RESOLVED) emission is preceded by DIRTY in the same wave; the dispatcher synthesizes a [DIRTY] prefix when the caller omits it and the node is not already dirty; raw and framed emission paths are observationally identical on the wire
rationale: glitch-free two-phase contract; D9 mechanism is impl freedom but the DIRTY-before-DATA ordering is observable

statement: DIRTY (phase 1) propagates through the entire reachable graph before DATA/RESOLVED (phase 2) begins — glitch-free diamond. Activation exemption: a compute fn's first run during subscribe() does not require a preceding DIRTY
rationale: two-phase push guarantees a fan-in node sees all settled deps before recompute

statement: diamond/fan-in: D recomputes exactly once after all changed deps settle in same wave
rationale: the spec only describes observable behavior; the mechanism (dirtyMask) is impl freedom

statement: the equals substitution (DATA→RESOLVED) fires only when there is exactly 1 DATA within the wave; 0 is irrelevant; with ≥2 they are all DATA. Within one wave at one node the tier-3 slot is ≥1 DATA XOR exactly 1 RESOLVED — never mixed (tier-3 wave exclusivity). Default equals = Object.is/is; custom equals via node opts; never invoked while cache is SENTINEL
rationale: multiple DATA yield no skip-fn benefit; exclusivity keeps cache coherent with last-delivered DATA -- RETIRED by D49 (Opt-3: no auto-equals-substitution; replaced by R-resolved-undirty)

statement: multiple settle-class messages on one node in one wave are resolved by tier-sort (DATA advances cache, a trailing INVALIDATE clears it; subscribers observe the full sequence). The sole explicit merge rule is INVALIDATE+INVALIDATE collapse (cleanup hook fires at most once). DATA+RESOLVED in the same wave on the same node is a protocol violation (R-resolved-undirty / D49)
rationale: tier ordering produces the right end-state without silently eliding messages

statement: INVALIDATE is broadcast at most once per node per wave (diamond fan-in cascades it once, not once per arriving path); an INVALIDATE arriving at an already-reset OR never-populated cache is a no-op — neither the cleanup hook nor the downstream broadcast fires again
rationale: prevents double-cleanup and wedged-DIRTY deadlock; the two reset states are observationally equivalent downstream

statement: SENTINEL = absence-of-DATA, protocol-decidable; the concrete sentinel value is per-language (TS undefined/Rust None/Py sentinel)

push-on-subscribe: in the SENTINEL state push [START]; in the dirty state push [START,DIRTY]; cached DATA is pushed to the new subscriber. START is the handshake — the first message any sink receives on a subscription, emitted before any other downstream delivery, not forwarded through intermediate nodes. EXCEPTION (R-pull / D55): a pull-mode node while QUIET pushes [START] ONLY — its cached value is NOT pushed on subscribe (it stays silent until demanded).

terminal-is-forever by default; resubscribable opt-in triggers a fresh-lifecycle reset. A late subscribe to a non-resubscribable terminal node is REJECTED (idiomatic error); to a resubscribable terminal node it resets the lifecycle (clears terminal/has-fired-once/DepRecords, drains pause lockset, re-arms first-run gate) before installing the sink. TEARDOWN does not block reset
rationale: D17; resubscribable IS the property gating late-subscribe re-activation

statement: completeWhenDepsComplete (default true): node auto-emits COMPLETE when ALL deps are TERMINAL — each dep has reached COMPLETE *or* an ABSORBED ERROR (errorWhenDepsError:false); an absorbed-error dep COUNTS as terminal-done (it is settled — no more input can arrive), it does NOT block completion (B42). Completion is 'all deps TERMINAL', NOT 'all deps Complete' and NOT 'ANY' (combineLatest semantics — fires once all sources settle). errorWhenDepsError (default true): node auto-emits ERROR when any dep errors (this auto-ERROR fires BEFORE the complete-check, so an error-terminal dep only reaches the completion logic when errorWhenDepsError:false has absorbed it). Terminal-emission operators (last/reduce) set completeWhenDepsComplete:false; rescue/catch operators set errorWhenDepsError:false and read ctx.depRecords[i].terminal explicitly. SCOPE: a dep TERMINAL = COMPLETE | ERROR; TEARDOWN is a destroy-cascade (tears the node down, not a settle) and does NOT count (B33-adjacent, out of scope). IMPL (TWO parts): (1) _allDepsComplete counts a TERMINAL dep as done — block only on a LIVE dep (TS `dep_terminal === undefined` blocks; NOT `!== true/Complete`), Rust all_deps_complete mirrors. (2) BOTH the COMPLETE receive-arm AND the absorbed-ERROR receive-arm (errorWhenDepsError:false) must check `completeWhenDepsComplete && all-deps-terminal -> COMPLETE`: the COMPLETE arm already does, but the ERROR-absorbed arm currently routes straight to _settleAfterAbsorbedTerminal/_maybeRun WITHOUT the check, so an absorbed-error dep terminating LAST would not fire the cascade — it must MIRROR the COMPLETE arm's check (Rust receive_from_dep ERROR arm same). Order-independent: whichever terminal lands last triggers the auto-COMPLETE.
rationale: effect/derived completion is the join of all deps reaching a terminal state — once every dep is terminal (Complete or absorbed-Error) no more input can arrive, so the node MUST settle (COMPLETE); rescue needs explicit terminal handling. B42 fix: the prior 'all deps Complete' (TS _allDepsComplete `tm!==true`, Rust all_deps_complete) wedged a node whose errorWhenDepsError:false dep ERRORed (terminal=payload≠Complete) — it never auto-completed even after all OTHER deps completed. Counting an absorbed-error dep as terminal-done fixes the wedge AND lets a rescue/catch operator with completeWhenDepsComplete:true auto-COMPLETE after recovery (RxJS catchError(()=>of(x)) parity). NOT hit by the landed catalog (rescue/race/sample use completeWhenDepsComplete:false so the auto-cascade is skipped → zero behavior change; a dep error on a default errorWhenDepsError:true node auto-ERRORs before the complete-check) — a pure latent-wedge fix. FLIPPED ACTIVE 2026-05-30 on the TS-arm-green (C-17 a/b/c ts:pass) + formal (wave_deps_complete.tla TLC-green + mutation-verified) precedent, like R-terminal-settles-dirty/R-rewire; rust+py arms (C-17 rust/py) follow in CSP-6/7.

statement: ctx.up is control-tier only (DIRTY/PAUSE/RESUME/INVALIDATE/TEARDOWN); DATA/RESOLVED/COMPLETE/ERROR are down-only
rationale: directional semantics; added in DR-5

statement: node = thinnest primitive: holds fn handle + deps + wave state machine (dep_records, dirty_mask, pending_count, cache, status, subscribers, pause_lockset); ZERO inspection cruft. Bare node() works at the substrate level but loses naming/find/describe — those are graph-layer
rationale: D5 Node↔Graph responsibility split; thin node ports cleanly to Rust

statement: node exposes: cache (readonly getter, never throws, never triggers computation), status, down(msgs), up(msgs) (restricted to control tier per R-ctx-up), subscribe(sink)→unsubscribe. cache replaces the old get()
rationale: D5 minimal node surface; D8 up/down boundary

statement: status ∈ {sentinel, pending, dirty, settled, resolved, completed, errored}; status is the source of truth for cache freshness (dirty → stale prior value, settled/resolved → fresh, completed/errored → final). cache never throws, never computes
rationale: D5 inspection reads status not raw cache

statement: state node (no deps) retains cache across disconnect — value is intrinsic/non-volatile (ROM). Compute node (deps and/or fn) clears cache on deactivation → status sentinel (RAM); reconnect re-runs fn from scratch with cleared DepRecords
rationale: D5; compute value is a function of live subscriptions

statement: node fn = (ctx)=>void; ctx = {up(msgs), down(msgs), depRecords[{latest, tier, prevData, terminal}], state, onDeactivation, onInvalidate}. NO return-value framing — all emission is explicit via ctx.down. Sugar (derived/effect/operator) value-level fn is wrapped to a ctx-fn in the graph layer at register time; node/producer are ctx-level (intentional tier power surface, DR-1)
rationale: D8 ctx.up/down; D27 sugar→ctx-fn conversion strictly in graph layer feeds behavioral parity

statement: two cleanup hooks: ctx.onDeactivation(fn) (release external resources on deactivation) + ctx.onInvalidate(fn) (flush on INVALIDATE). onRerun (0 callsites) and onResubscribableReset (1 callsite → absorbed by ctx.state lifecycle) are cut. fn return value is freed for sugar mapping. PER-RUN LIFECYCLE (D28 clarification): both hook lists are CLEARED before each fn invocation and re-registered by the fn body — only the LATEST run's registrations are live (React effect-cleanup model). A re-run SUPERSEDES the prior run's hooks; superseded registrations are DISCARDED WITHOUT firing (consistent with the cut onRerun — there is no fire-on-rerun hook). So after K fn runs, an INVALIDATE fires onInvalidate exactly once (the current run's), and deactivation fires onDeactivation exactly once (NOT K times). Contract: a fn must (re-)register its cleanup on EVERY run that needs it (a registration guarded to a single run is dropped on the next run). A single-run node keeps its single registration (no re-run = no clear). deactivate() fires the live onDeactivation hooks then clears both lists.
rationale: D28; internal state reset belongs to ctx.state lifecycle, cleanup hooks only manage external resources + INVALIDATE. Per-run clear (D28 clarification) fixes the push-only accumulation bug surfaced by the CSP-5 Rust /qa (finding E, parity-consistent in both arms): re-registering each run grew the hook list unbounded and fired K stale hooks on the K-th INVALIDATE. Uniform clear-and-re-register for BOTH hooks (user-approved 2026-05-29); discard-without-firing keeps D28's onRerun-cut (fire-on-rerun would resurrect it).

statement: ctx.state = per-node private cross-wave state (implicit OK — node-private, not shared). Default fresh-lifecycle wipe; ctx.state.persist(on?) keeps across lifecycle. Shared/observable state must be an explicit node + dep (not ctx.state). INVALIDATE is lifecycle-continue (not fresh-lifecycle) so it does NOT wipe ctx.state — manual flush via onInvalidate
rationale: D23 private state OK, shared memory explicit; D29 fresh-lifecycle wipe + persist

statement: compute fn first-fires only after every declared dep has settled (delivered ≥1 real DATA this or a prior wave) under partial:false — producing one combined initial wave. partial:true turns the gate OFF (fn fires as soon as dirty-dep-count hits 0; fn body MUST guard SENTINEL per dep). terminalAsRealInput:true also lets a dep terminal settle the gate (Reduce-class). The gate is first-run-only (has-called-fn-once); INVALIDATE does not re-arm it; a resubscribable terminal reset does
rationale: clean multi-dep activation handshake without phantom partial waves

statement: initial (non-SENTINEL): pre-populates cache and a source pushes [DATA,initial] on subscribe; first emit runs equals against initial. Absent/undefined initial → cache holds SENTINEL, no push-on-subscribe, first emit is always DATA. INVALIDATE and resetOnTeardown return cache to SENTINEL
rationale: D16 sentinel semantics; initial is T|null never T|undefined

statement: dynamicNode = node construction variant (NOT a verb): declares a superset of all possible deps at construction, fn reads a subset per invocation via track(dep). All declared deps participate in wave tracking; an unread dep's update fires the fn (a ctx-fn with explicit ctx.down). The fn DECIDES whether to propagate: it inspects which deps delivered this wave (ctx.depRecords[i].batch) and either re-emits via ctx.down (DATA) OR early-returns to stay QUIET, in which case the substrate synthesizes ONE undirty RESOLVED (D49: RESOLVED = UNDIRTY) that clears the downstream dirty WITHOUT a redundant DATA (D53). The suppress-vs-propagate decision on an unread-dep change is use-case-dependent, so it belongs to the fn (D53), NOT an automatic substrate read-mask (REJECTED D53 -- it would hard-code one policy and be the lone exception to D49's opt-in-dedup-everywhere). A downstream distinctUntilChanged remains an alternative for value-based dedup. track() is a pure per-invocation value-reader (depRecords[i].latest). Same first-run gate as static nodes. Intra-graph only — cross-graph deps go through the wire bridge (no inter-graph dynamicNode)
rationale: D35 distinct from rewire (per-invocation read-selection vs dep-set mutation); D22 bounds tracked deps to one causal domain

statement: PAUSE/RESUME carry a lock_id; lockset semantics: a true resume occurs only when every lock has RESUMEd; same-id is idempotent; RESUME of an unknown lock is a no-op (D59) The routing of a RESUME for a lock NOT held HERE is governed by R-up-routing -- it FORWARDS up the declared cone to find the holder (release-if-held-else-forward-up) rather than a flat no-op; a lock no node up the cone holds drops at the depless-source terminus (net no-op). The held-release/idempotent/every-lock-resumed lockset semantics above are unchanged.

pausable {true | 'resumeAll' | false}. true (default): skip fn while any lock held, fire fn once on final-lock RESUME with latest dep values; a leaf source's (depless) own external down() -- sync OR async (timer tick / promise resolve / state.set) -- is NOT gated in default mode (delivered immediately). 'resumeAll': buffer the node's own tier-3/4 settle slice while paused (incl a leaf source's own sync/async down()), replay per-entry in arrival order on final-lock RESUME against a pre-pause baseline (equals references the conceptual-timeline cache); tier-5/6 bypass the buffer. false: ignore PAUSE/RESUME ENTIRELY (timer sources that must keep producing) -- the lockset is never consulted, neither dep-driven recompute nor any (sync/async) own production is gated or buffered. pausable mode is the OUTER gate over R-async-paused (D44): an async-pool late emit buffers ONLY when pausable in {true,'resumeAll'} AND (for true) the node is a COMPUTE node (deps>0); a depless async leaf source delivers immediately in true mode (leaf-vs-compute discriminator = deps.length===0). The ORTHOGONAL pull axis (NodeOptions.pull:true, R-pull / D55) sits ON TOP of pausable mode: a pull node is quiet-by-default (self-holds a per-node demand lock) and RE-QUIETS after each demand pulse; while quiet it suppresses the downstream DIRTY relay + push-on-subscribe; the pausable mode then determines the DEMAND DELIVERY CONTENT (true → coalesced latest; 'resumeAll' → buffered backlog drained). pull+pausable:false is REJECTED (pull needs RESUME as the demand signal).
rationale: PAUSE is backpressure on recomputation/propagation; production-gating is resumeAll's job. D44 pins the precedence over R-async-paused -- production is gated only by resumeAll, never by true/false (formal wave_async_paused.tla: ShouldBuffer + NoBufferWhenIgnoring, TLC-green across true/false/leaf/resumeAll + mutation-verified). D55 adds the orthogonal pull axis (delivery-content = mode).

statement: an async result arriving at a paused node buffers and replays on final-lock RESUME -- BUT this is GATED by pausable mode (D44), not unconditional: it applies only when pausable in {true,'resumeAll'} and, in true mode, only to a COMPUTE node (deps>0). A pausable:false node never buffers (ignores PAUSE, keeps producing); a true-mode depless leaf source delivers its own async production immediately (R-pause-modes). The buffered result enters the node-level pause_lockset-scoped buffer (lock_id scope = node-level pause_lockset).
rationale: DR-3; D44 conditions the buffering on pausable mode + node kind -- the C-2 node is an async COMPUTE node (deps>0), which is why it buffers; pausable:false (B20) and the async leaf source (B20's twin) are the cases the unconditional reading got wrong.

statement: a [[TEARDOWN]] arriving at a non-terminal node synthesizes a [COMPLETE] prefix in the same wave ([[COMPLETE],[TEARDOWN]]) so bridge subscribers resolve before unwiring. Idempotent (subsequent TEARDOWN arrives alone); skipped when the wave already carries COMPLETE/ERROR
rationale: clean complete-then-teardown lifecycle pair; firstValueFrom-style bridges need the COMPLETE

statement: replayBuffer:N → node keeps a circular buffer of the last N outgoing DATA values; a late subscriber receives buffered DATA after the START handshake and before live updates
rationale: replaces the replay() operator + subscribe-hook monkeypatching

statement: restore ≠ fresh-lifecycle: snapshot serializes all ctx.state; restore restores everything (no wipe); wipe occurs only on a fresh-lifecycle transition
rationale: Flag 1; added in DR-5

statement: snapshot = topology + cache + factory-name refs (NOT fn bodies — the fn lives in code). restore re-resolves nodes by factory name via the dispatcher registry; an anonymous inline fn (no name) is marked local-only and cannot restore cross-process (honestly labeled). Incremental restore via changeset. Storage tiers / WAL / codec / envelope are presentation-layer + deferred, not substrate rules
rationale: D25; fn cannot serialize, factory-registry re-resolution model

statement: Graph = convenience + inspection entry: register/name/find/describe/observe/profile/snapshot/mount/batch/operators. g.* sugar desugars to dispatcher.register + Node + auto-registers into the graph inspection index. Graph is optional convenience, not a mandatory container; multi-graph is natural
rationale: D5 Graph holds all convenience+inspection; D3 graph-first mental anchor

statement: edges are derived on-demand from each node's CURRENT/LIVE deps (the node's live _deps, RE-READ at describe() call time — NOT a construction-time snapshot, so a rewire C-8/C-11 is reflected; D51) + the mount hierarchy; there is no stored edge registry and no connect/disconnect. Every edge shown in describe has a real protocol subscription behind it — decorative edges are not representable (the live-deps reading is what KEEPS this true post-rewire: a construction-time edge would be decorative after removeDep). A live dep absent from the graph inspection index (a runtime *Map inner / bare graph-less node) is auto-discovered as a snapshot node, factory from its NodeOptions.factory (R-describe).
rationale: D3 topology is a pure function of (nodes, CURRENT deps, mounts); D51 — 'construction-time deps' self-contradicted 'every edge has a real subscription' once rewire (D42/D47) made topology dynamic (a removeDep'd construction edge is decorative). Live-deps reading restores truthfulness + realizes D47/C-11 'describe shows currently-live inners'.

statement: setDeps/addDep/removeDep = runtime topology rewire, INTRA-graph only (D22 single causal domain; no inter-graph form — cross-graph wiring is only via the wire bridge). Surgical/Option-C: a dep in both old and new sets is left untouched (subscription + DepRecord survive); only removed deps unsubscribe + discard their DepRecord, only added deps fresh-subscribe; DepRecord-ref dispatch lets kept deps reorder freely. Across a rewire: the first-run gate (_hasCalledFnOnce) is PRESERVED, never re-armed (re-arming would re-gate unchanged deps); an added dep enters prevData=SENTINEL and the fn guards via prevData===SENTINEL; the activated compute-node cache is PRESERVED (R-rom-ram); pause lockset + buffer PRESERVED. An added dep with a cached DATA pushes [DIRTY,DATA] on subscribe (R-push-subscribe); a SENTINEL dep delivers START only. removeDep clears the removed dep's dirty contribution; if it was the sole dirty contributor and the node was dirty, the wave auto-settles. A removed dep's queued messages (DIRTY/DATA/INVALIDATE) are DRAINED — nothing strands downstream. Rejects: self-dependency; a cycle (DFS O(V+E)); a terminal this (completed/errored); adding a non-resubscribable terminal dep (would wedge — resubscribable terminal deps are allowed). removeDep to zero deps is allowed (degenerate fn-no-deps; cache preserved; no auto-deactivate). Mid-wave rewire (between dep deliveries) is allowed; mid-fn rewire (while the node's fn is executing, _insideRunWave) and reentrant rewire (another setDeps/addDep/removeDep in flight) are REJECTED — a fn mutating its own topology mid-wave is the synchronous feedback-cycle ERROR (D37/R-reentrancy). Topology change does not bump a version counter (topology ≠ DATA). Every rewire API requires an explicit fn (fn-deps pairing: user fns read data[i]/prevData[i] positionally, so a dep-shape change must re-declare the fn). A SELF-triggered mutation (a fn changing its OWN deps in response to its own data) must use the deferred ctx.rewireNext path (R-rewire-deferred / D47), NOT an immediate in-fn call.
rationale: D42 ratifies the TLA+-verified (port-model wave_protocol_rewire, 126k states) rewire design Q1–Q7 for the clean-slate substrate; D22 bounds it to one causal domain; the mid-fn reject is floor-mandated by D37/R-reentrancy; surgical/Option-C + required-fn come from the Phase 13.8 design iteration. Per D42 SD-2, the cross-axis formal coverage is COMPLETE (wave_rewire.tla INVALIDATE+terminal + wave_rewire_emit.tla equals+multi-sink, all TLC-green + mutation-verified) and the TS C-8 arm is green; flipped ACTIVE 2026-05-28 on the TS-arm-green+formal precedent (R-reentrancy/R-up-at-source/R-dirty-before-data), rust/py conformance arms tracked separately in C-8 runtimes

statement: graph.mount(subgraph,{at}) embeds a child graph addressable under the parent namespace (:: delimited paths); lifecycle signals propagate parent→mounted children; mount has no deps (exempt from deps-first ordering)
rationale: D4 mount verb; L4-Q4 mount exemption

statement: describe(opts?) = static, JSON-serializable structure snapshot: {name?; nodes:DNode[]; edges:{from,to}[]; subgraphs?}. DNode = {id (stable mount-aware :: path, auto-numbered when unnamed), name?, factory (operator real name per D6/L1.5, not 'derived'), status (R-status-enum), value? (field ABSENT = SENTINEL/never-emitted), deps:id[], meta? (static annotations, R-meta-presentation)}. edges are derived from each node's CURRENT/LIVE deps + the mount hierarchy (R-edges-derived / D51) — re-read at call time, so a rewire (C-8 immediate / C-11 *Map deferred) is reflected (the snapshot is point-in-time live, NOT a construction snapshot). A live dep absent from the graph index (a runtime *Map inner / bare graph-less node) is AUTO-DISCOVERED as a snapshot node: synthesized stable id, status/value from the node getters, factory from its OWN NodeOptions.factory (the field D43 reserved for standalone graph-less operators, set by the free initNode) else '?'; auto-discovered inners are NOT persistently registered in the graph index (best-effort live capture, no register/unregister churn — D51 chose B2 over a persistent registry; first cut discovers ONE level, transitive = follow-up). value carries the cache snapshot at call time; fn bodies are never serialized (factory-name ref only, D25). describe({explain:{from,to}}) = causal-chain subset (same shape, filtered to the from→to chain). Renderers (pretty/mermaid/d2) are pure functions over the snapshot — NOT methods and NOT a describe({format}) option; there is no graph.explain(). Live-topology streaming (rewire deltas) is an observe topology-event, deferred to CSP-2 viz
rationale: D3 describe first-class; D39 pins the field set; L4-Q8 renderers pure fns; D25 snapshot same source; per-language (D24, never in parity — documented contract, not conformance-tested); D51 — the snapshot reflects LIVE deps (truthful post-rewire) + auto-discovers unregistered inners (factory via the D43-reserved NodeOptions.factory); live-topology STREAMING (deltas) stays deferred to viz (a point-in-time read is not streaming)

statement: observe(path?) = read-only live message tap returning a subscribable EGRESS ({subscribe(sink)→unsubscribe}) — NOT a graph node (no self-observation island). observe is a REAL (lazily-activating) subscriber: it uses subscribe internally, so observing a COLD node activates it + its upstream (running their fns), and observing a cached node receives the [DATA,cached] push (R-push-subscribe). 'Read-only' (D19) means observe never EMITS or MUTATES node state — it does NOT mean activation-free; observing a cold graph activates it. Each stream item is an enveloped ObserveEvent = {path, msg (the Message), tier (messageTier), seq (graph-local monotonic clock, D26)}; the envelope carries node identity so single-node / subtree / whole-graph observe share ONE shape. Upstream control is a separate Graph affordance: single-node up(msgs) / all-nodes up(path,msgs) (e.g. PAUSE); a node guard denying an upstream message drops it silently (R-up-at-source)
rationale: D5 Graph IS the introspection layer; D39 pins the ObserveEvent envelope + read-only egress (not a node); D19 inspection read-only; per-language (D24, never in parity)

statement: inspection surface = describe (incl explain mode) + observe + profile — 3 first-class methods on Graph; no separate Inspector object
rationale: L4-Q8 inspection consolidation

statement: meta companion stores are presentation/graph-layer, NOT substrate. Static annotations (description/type/range/format/access/tags/unit) → describe metadata attached via g.node opts. Reactive annotations (a status/error that changes over time) → explicit nodes + dep (R-ctx-state / D23). The substrate node carries zero meta machinery. meta.owner ABAC is presentation/multi-agent, out of substrate scope
rationale: D36; D5 node=thinnest, meta is annotation feeding describe (graph owns inspection)

statement: graph.signal(msgs) broadcasts a message to all registered nodes (e.g. [[PAUSE,lockId]] or [[INVALIDATE]]); graph.destroy() broadcasts [[TEARDOWN]]. graph.set(name,v) = node.down([[DATA,v]]) sugar; graph.get(name) = cache read
rationale: D5 graph convenience; L4-Q1 state.set = node.down sugar

statement: monotonic time = a graph-local counter (causal-domain ordering, folded into the graph); wall-clock = a system call; there is NO global clock singleton
rationale: D26 / L3-Q9 config dissolution; graph = single-thread concurrency domain so ordering is domain-local (refined 2026-05-31 with D22 option-A; was 'causal domain', see R-graph-domain)

statement: all fn go through the dispatcher / FactoryRegistry; node((ctx)=>...) also runs through the LocalSync pool. There is no inline-fn-bypasses-dispatcher path
rationale: F-DISPATCH-ALL; sacred L0.7 (all fn through dispatcher)

statement: dispatcher.invoke is sync void — wave-state mutation always serializes onto the graph's single thread; async/remote execution returns via a pool callback. 1.0 pools = LocalSync + LocalAsync; dispatcher keeps a pluggable pool trait for WorkerPool/RemotePool
rationale: F-SYNC-CORE; D20 pool set; sacred L0.7 (wave protocol impl is sync)

statement: handle = pure data (pool_id, handle_id), NO methods — serializable/snapshottable/wire-transferable; it is a dispatcher-table index. node ≠ handle (node has up/down methods at the external-world boundary)
rationale: D7 handle is pure data

statement: graph = single-thread CONCURRENCY domain (the unit of concurrency, NOT the bound of causal influence). In-domain propagation is ONE synchronous causal wave: same-tick, glitch-free, diamonds RESOLVED-merged so a fan-in sees one consistent version of its source. Causal influence is NOT bounded by the graph — it CROSSES domains via the async wire bridge as DELAYED CONSISTENCY (a value produced in wave N is consumed one tick later in the peer domain; the two-phase wire gate preserves cross-domain consistency — wave_xgraph.tla L2.F). Compute parallelism is via pool callback (results serialize back to the domain's thread); true parallelism is via multiple graphs + wire bridge. Disjoint waves in the same graph do not parallelize (one concurrency domain = one dispatcher).
rationale: D22 wave protocol is lock-free because the graph boundary is the CONCURRENCY boundary. Wording refined 2026-05-31 (D22 option-A in-place edit; SESSION-reactive-linear-and-git M4): 'causal domain = concurrency domain' conflated two things — causal influence spans the wire bridge, so the graph bounds the concurrency unit, not the causal range; cross-domain causal propagation is delayed-consistency (wave_xgraph.tla L2.F two-phase gate). Behavior unchanged (C-1/C-4 unaffected).

statement: state changes propagate reactively via messages; never poll a node's value on a timer or busy-wait for status; periodic behavior is a reactive timer source emitting through the graph
rationale: spec §5.8 durable value

statement: no imperative side-channel triggers (event emitters, callbacks, setTimeout+set) to drive graph behavior; all coordination uses ctx.up signals + message flow through topology; remove imperative paths when no caller depends on them
rationale: spec §5.9 durable value (feedback_no_imperative)

statement: no bare async primitives in the reactive layer (TS: Promise/queueMicrotask/setTimeout/process.nextTick; PY: asyncio.create_task/threading.Timer/raw coroutines). Async boundaries live only in sources (fromPromise/fromAsyncIter) and the pool/runner layer
rationale: spec §5.10; F-SYNC-CORE async only at pool/wire boundary

statement: all data propagation — including initial values at connection time — flows through messages [[DATA,v]]; nodes do not peek a dep's .cache to seed computation; .cache is a read-only accessor for external consumers
rationale: spec §5.12 single mental model: if data moved, a message carried it

statement: protocol internals (DIRTY/RESOLVED/bitmask) never surface in the value-level primary API (derived/effect/operator); ctx-level primitives (node/producer) intentionally expose tier as a power surface (DR-1 §5.11 amend). A developer using value-level sugar never reads the spec to start
rationale: DR-1 ctx-level is a deliberate protocol-facing power surface; value-level is §5.11-compliant primary

statement: a synchronous feedback cycle — a node fn that, during its invocation, transitively re-drives one of its own (direct or indirect) deps so the same node's fn would re-enter before its wave completes — is a wave-level protocol ERROR. Detection is node-local and free: a node refuses to enter its fn-run while its own in-wave flag (_insideRunWave) is already set, and throws; the graph layer catches the throw and converts it to [[ERROR, e]] down (D30 — value-level throw → graph-layer ERROR), located at a node ON the cycle (the value-level catch nearest the throw on the synchronous unwind — implementation-determined, NOT necessarily the re-entered node), aborting the wave. The core neither queues nor bounds-then-runs the cycle (reject, not iterate). Legitimate accumulation uses per-node ctx.state (e.g. scan): not a topological cycle, never re-enters. Async feedback that crosses a turn boundary via an async pool is out of scope — it is not synchronous re-entry and does not desync the wave. No numeric rerun-depth cap is needed (precise in-wave flag detection supersedes the blunt maxFnRerunDepth)
rationale: D37; surfaced by CSP-1 /qa (backlog B10); reject (B) over queue-to-wave-end (A) because A normalizes imperative-control-flow-as-topology (feedback_no_imperative) and does not root-fix; detection reuses the existing _insideRunWave flag, dispatcher stays a pure funnel (F-DISPATCH-ALL), error ownership graph-level (D30)

statement: a depless source is the terminus of upstream control forwarding (R-ctx-up). It self-ACTS only on a message with a coherent round-trip action: INVALIDATE → HONOR the invalidate-request (clear cache to SENTINEL, fire onInvalidate, broadcast INVALIDATE downstream = self _invalidate; the down-cascade clears the reachable downstream cone; a node guard may deny it per R-observe, dropping silently). DIRTY → DROP/no-op (a source has no downstream-driven recompute; self-dirty would wedge downstream awaiting a settle that never arrives). TEARDOWN → DROP/no-op (source lifecycle is source/graph-owned; revisit on a real cascade-teardown-up consumer). Dep-bearing intermediate nodes never self-act on upstream control — they forward toward deps only; the source is the single actor and the down-cascade is the effect (D59/R-up-routing) A forwarded RESUME (a routed pull DEMAND, R-pull) whose pullId this depless source does NOT hold -> DROP at the terminus, like DIRTY; a source that DOES hold the pullId (a pull source) releases its quiet lock and FIRES one delivery (R-pull). Dep-bearing intermediates forward an unheld RESUME up toward deps (release-if-held-else-forward-up), never self-acting.
rationale: D38; B11; R-ctx-up/DR-5 lists INVALIDATE up-allowed and the only self-consistent reason is terminus honoring (DS-1 L1.11 'invalidate-request'); INVALIDATE-up is a cache-drop request not an imperative write, so it respects no-imperative + source-owns-value; DIRTY/TEARDOWN lack a coherent terminus action

statement: profile(opts?) = opt-in accumulated-counter snapshot: {waves; nodes:Record<path, NodeProfile>}, NodeProfile = {invokes, emits, resolved, errored, lastDurationNs?, totalDurationNs?}. Counters are backed by an opt-in dispatcher/graph-level recorder (DS-1 inspectorEnabled / globalInspector→dispatcher hook), NEVER stored on the thin node (R-node-thin); the dispatcher is the invoke funnel (F-DISPATCH-ALL) so it is the natural source of invoke counts + fn duration. Default OFF = zero runtime overhead (F-PERF). profile is a point-in-time snapshot (like describe); a streaming profile is an observe-aggregation, not a new mechanism. Shares the mount-aware :: path key with describe/observe
rationale: D39; L4-Q8 third inspection method; R-node-thin keeps counters off the node; F-DISPATCH-ALL dispatcher sees every invoke; F-PERF opt-in; per-language (D24, never in parity)

statement: A node fn may, DURING its run, request a mutation of its OWN dep set via ctx.rewireNext(op), op in {addDep(node,fn) | removeDep(node,fn) | setDeps(nodes,fn)} (R-rewire surgical/Option-C semantics, D42). The request is QUEUED, not applied in place; the dispatcher DRAINS the queue at the COMMITTED wave boundary — after the current wave settles, and after a batch() commits or the final-lock RESUME (never on an un-committed or paused view) — applying each mutation as a fresh wave. Drain order is deterministic: per-node FIFO in issue order, nodes drained in causal order. This deferral is the ONLY legal self-triggered rewire: IMMEDIATE in-fn self-rewire remains the D37 mid-fn feedback-cycle ERROR (R-reentrancy); rewireNext moves application to a turn boundary where _insideRunWave is false. An added dep with cached DATA pushes [DIRTY,DATA] on the boundary wave (R-push-subscribe); a removed dep is unsubscribed and DRAINED, and if it loses its last subscriber it _deactivates and fires onDeactivation (input-side teardown — the basis for operator cancellation / abortInFlight). The first-run gate is PRESERVED across a deferred rewire (never re-armed, R-rewire). If the node goes terminal during the wave, its pending rewireNext queue is discarded. A rewireNext producing no net dep-set change is a no-op; a net-changing rewireNext re-issued every boundary (oscillation) is a user-level runaway (like an infinite producer), not a substrate-detected error. The wave-boundary drain ALSO hosts a SELF-TRIGGERED DEMAND — a CONE-ROUTED RESUME(pullId) demand to a pull-mode node (R-pull / R-up-routing / D55,D59), not only dep-set mutations — for the same D37-avoidance reason (an immediate in-fn demand whose delivery loops back re-enters the consumer); same committed-boundary drain, same deferral semantics. INTRA-graph only (D22).
rationale: D47; *Map operators must grow/shrink their own dep set in response to their own data; the D37 mid-fn reject + the async-pool probe (the async pool does NOT defer the fn — _insideRunWave is set during any fn run, dispatcher/index.ts:48 + node.ts:692) leave the wave boundary as the only legal application point. removeDep is the only thing that stops an abandoned inner's source (read-gate masks output only). Complements R-rewire (external/immediate) with a self/deferred form, reusing its surgical semantics. FLIPPED ACTIVE 2026-05-30 on the TS-arm-green + formal precedent (wave_rewire_deferred.tla TLC-green 5056 states + 4 invariants mutation-verified; B15 fn-swap-handle-GC landed = SD-2 prereq met): TS impl = batch/boundary.ts wave-owner depth counter + deferred-drain FIFO (the TS analogue of the Rust WaveScope/B25), node.ts ctx.rewireNext + boundary-bracketed subscribe/down/up/ctx.down/ctx.up/batch; C-11 ts:pass (conformance.test.ts 6 facets + rewire-deferred.test.ts 8 units). rust/py arms last (CSP-5/7). Batch/pause cross-axis drain timing = backlog B24; describe-renders-live-inners (R-edges-derived construction-deps tension) = backlog B34. D55 reuses this boundary to host a self-triggered pull DEMAND (R-pull).

statement: RESOLVED is the UNDIRTY / no-occurrence settle: a node DIRTY'd in phase 1 that produces NO tier-3 value this wave emits exactly one RESOLVED to clear the downstream dirty (filter-reject / no-emit fn, zero-dep un-dirty, INVALIDATE at a never-populated cache, batch-rollback DIRTY-balance). RESOLVED NEVER substitutes for a DATA and NEVER signals 'value unchanged' -- every value-occurrence is emitted as DATA regardless of value-equality (no auto-equals-substitution; the substrate does not inspect per-wave DATA count for substitution). The undirty RESOLVED is SUBSTRATE-SYNTHESIZED: a value-level operator simply returns without emitting and the substrate emits the balancing RESOLVED (R-primary-api-clean -- operator bodies carry no protocol tier); an operator MAY emit its own DATA/RESOLVED explicitly as an escape hatch. Tier-3 wave exclusivity holds: one node's settle this wave is >=1 DATA (occurrence) XOR exactly 1 RESOLVED (undirty), never mixed. RESOLVED is preceded by DIRTY in the same wave (R-dirty-before-data) like DATA. Dedup (suppress an unchanged emission / skip an expensive recompute) is OPT-IN at the operator layer (distinctUntilChanged / fn early-return), never a substrate behavior; NodeOptions.equals does not exist.
rationale: D49 supersedes D15/R-equals: equals-absorption overloaded RESOLVED (occurrence-unchanged vs dirty-clear) and destroyed occurrence info, breaking event-counting operators. Narrowing RESOLVED to undirty-only keeps occurrences as DATA (take/scan/snapshot correct) and simplifies the emit path. Glitch-free diamond (R-two-phase/R-diamond) is orthogonal and preserved.

statement: INVALIDATE × PAUSE precedence (default/'true' mode). A dep's INVALIDATE arriving while a compute node N is paused: (1) PROPAGATES downstream immediately (consistent with immediate DIRTY — not buffered in default mode; the downstream's N-DIRTY is balanced by this INVALIDATE's dirty-clear); (2) SUPERSEDES that dep's buffered paused dep-wave — N clears the dep to SENTINEL + drops its pending change, then re-derives the pending-recompute flag from whether ANY dep still carries a buffered value-change (ATTRIBUTED). On final-lock RESUME N recomputes once with the latest dep values ONLY if some dep still has a live buffered change; if none remains the recompute is CANCELLED (N already settled to SENTINEL via its own INVALIDATE — it never recomputes against an all-SENTINEL dep set). A later DATA on the same dep re-arms the buffer ([DATA,INVALIDATE,DATA2] → recompute with DATA2). resumeAll mode buffers+replays tier-3/4 on its own path; this rule is the default-mode coalesce semantics.
rationale: D50; the INVALIDATE-side analogue of D44 (async×PAUSE). Prevents a spurious recompute against a vanished input — a redundant undirty RESOLVED (guarded fn) or a spurious terminal ERROR (non-guarding fn → panic → D30). Attributed cancellation preserves multi-dep updates (no lost update). Formal wave_paused_invalidate.tla (ChangedImpliesLive + PendingReflectsChanges + NoAllSentinelRecompute), TLC-green + mutation-verified. FLIPPED ACTIVE 2026-05-29 on the TS+Rust-arms-green + formal precedent (C-13 ts:pass+rust:pass, both impl-fixes teeth-verified); py arm CSP-7.

statement: A dep's TERMINAL (COMPLETE/ERROR) RELEASES that dep's outstanding in-wave DIRTY contribution: if the dep went DIRTY this wave (phase 1) and has NOT yet settled with DATA/RESOLVED, the receiving node clears that dep's dirty flag and decrements its pending count — exactly as the DATA/RESOLVED/INVALIDATE arms do. This is the EXACTLY-ONE-SETTLE invariant: every dep that goes DIRTY in phase 1 has its contribution released in phase 2 by exactly one settle-class event in {DATA, RESOLVED, INVALIDATE, COMPLETE, ERROR}. It applies in the ABSORBED-terminal cases where the node stays live — completeWhenDepsComplete:false (last/reduce, the *Map higher-order operators) and errorWhenDepsError:false (rescue/catch, R-deps-terminal); the AUTO-CASCADE cases (completeWhenDepsComplete && all deps complete -> node COMPLETE; errorWhenDepsError && a dep errors -> node ERROR) make the node itself terminal, so pending is moot there. If releasing the terminal dep's contribution drains pending to 0 while the node has already broadcast DIRTY this wave AND no terminal cascade fires, the node SETTLES: it recomputes (-> DATA from the remaining live deps' latest values) or, producing no tier-3 value, the substrate synthesizes exactly one undirty RESOLVED (R-resolved-undirty) to balance the downstream DIRTY. WITHOUT this release, a dep that emits DIRTY-then-COMPLETE/ERROR-without-a-value strands pending>0 -> the node never recomputes/settles and the DIRTY it broadcast wedges the downstream cone (the deadlock R-invalidate-idempotent already prevents for the INVALIDATE case). Restores R-diamond / R-two-phase for a diamond whose one leg terminates mid-wave. SCOPE: COMPLETE/ERROR only; a TEARDOWN arriving at a dirtied dep is the terminal-relay question (R-teardown-complete / B33), out of scope here.
rationale: surfaced by the CSP-2.7 /qa (edge-case review of the *Map operators): node._receiveFromDep's COMPLETE/ERROR arms did not clear a dep's dirty contribution the way the DATA/RESOLVED/INVALIDATE arms do, so a DIRTY-then-terminal-without-DATA dep wedged a multi-dep node (B35). Pins TERMINAL as a settle-class event for dirty-accounting — the missing exactly-one-settle invariant — mirroring the INVALIDATE wedge-guard (the EC3 fix). Locked via /design-review (recommendation A-via-partial-C: a shared release-dirty + post-settle-undirty helper called by COMPLETE/ERROR alongside DATA/RESOLVED). PRE-EXISTING latent gap since CSP-1 (NOT introduced by D47); parity-consistent — the Rust dep-terminal receive arm is not yet built (node.rs _ => {}), so lock-BEFORE-build. No new D# (a dirty-accounting clarification of the two-phase contract D9, surfaced under D30 terminal handling). Formal: wave_terminal_dirty.tla (PendingCountsDirty + NoWedge, mutation-verified — dropping the terminal's release trips PendingCountsDirty). FLIPPED ACTIVE 2026-05-30 on the TS-arm-green + formal precedent (R-rewire/R-reentrancy/R-rewire-deferred): TS impl = node.ts _receiveFromDep COMPLETE/ERROR arms _releaseDepDirty(idx) + _settleAfterAbsorbedTerminal (sawData→recompute, else undirty RESOLVED) / _maybeRun for terminalAsRealInput; C-15 ts:pass (a/b/c). rust:todo = the CSP-6 dep-terminal slice (builds the propagation machinery WITH the release first time, lock-before-build); py:todo CSP-7.

statement: pull-mode node (NodeOptions.pullId:<LockId> -- an author-supplied UNIQUE Symbol written verbatim into the demander's fn; NEVER the node name (non-load-bearing debug metadata), NEVER a bare string (string-equality collides with a same-string pause lock); REPLACES the D55 pull:true boolean) = a quiet-until-demanded source; the demand is a RESUME (NO new message type -- R-msg-closed-set's 10-message set is intact). QUIET (default -- the node self-holds its pullId as its demand lock): (1) ABSORBS an upstream DIRTY WITHOUT relaying it downstream -- internal per-dep dirty/pending accounting is kept, only the DOWNSTREAM DIRTY broadcast is suppressed (the WEDGE FIX); (2) does NOT push-on-subscribe its cached value (START only) -- overrides R-push-subscribe while quiet; (3) tracks dep changes per its ORTHOGONAL pausable mode (true -> coalesce to latest; 'resumeAll' -> buffer the backlog). DEMAND = a CONE-ROUTED RESUME of the node's pullId (R-up-routing): the demander issues ctx.up([[RESUME, pullId]]) (broadcast up the declared cone) or ctx.up(towardDep, [[RESUME, pullId]]) (directed first-hop prune) WITHOUT holding the node's reference; the RESUME travels up declared edges to the pullId-holder, matched by SYMBOL IDENTITY (zero collision; siblings disambiguated). The holder fires EXACTLY ONE delivery then RE-QUIETS (1:1), emitting a fresh DIRTY-before-DATA wave (R-dirty-before-data) so the downstream dirty is balanced. Delivery CONTENT = the pausable mode: true -> the coalesced LATEST (one DATA); 'resumeAll' -> the buffered BACKLOG drained (first-demand backlog INCLUDES the activation value). A demand with NO intervening change -> NO delivery (silent). A demand arriving while a dep DIRTY is in flight (pending>0) fires once the node is settle-ready. pullId + pausable:false is REJECTED at construction (contradiction -- pull needs RESUME as the demand). A SELF-triggered demand (a consumer fn demanding a dep it ALSO reads) MUST defer to the committed wave boundary via R-rewire-deferred (D47) -- an immediate routed RESUME whose delivery loops back re-enters the consumer (D37/R-reentrancy); the consumer accepts one-wave latency. INTRA-graph only (D22). String-LABEL ergonomics (a label->pullId mint + a label->token registry with DUPLICATE-DETECTION) are graph-layer sugar (D6/D24). pull is SUBSTRATE (conformance C-16); the reactiveList two-port shape (stream push + snapshot pull) built on it is per-language (D6/D24, never parity).
rationale: D55 introduced the pull-mode node + delivery; D59 REVISES the TRIGGER/ROUTING + API (supersedes D55's per-node-opaque-symbol + direct-target ctx.demandNext, RETAINS delivery). A demand must reach the pull node WITHOUT a node reference -- a reference IS the .cache anti-pattern (reach the node, read .cache, an UNORDERED + invisible side-channel) -- so the demand is a RESUME routed up the DECLARED cone (R-up-routing): inspectable (describe/observe), wave-ORDERED (DIRTY-before-DATA), needs only the author-known pullId. RESUME reused (no new message): a pull node is a perpetually-self-paused node, a demand a momentary resume. pullId = author Symbol via pullId:<id> (identity match, zero collision; bare string collides with pause-lock strings; name is non-load-bearing); RESUME payload type LockId=string|symbol UNCHANGED. label ergonomics + duplicate-detection are graph-layer sugar. The original probe-verified delivery (P0b wedge -> absorb-DIRTY fix; P4/P5 matrix) is unchanged.

statement: Up-going control messages (R-ctx-up) route along DECLARED dep-edges. ctx.up(msgs) broadcasts up ALL deps; ctx.up(towardDep, msgs) routes up ONE declared edge (directed -- prunes other branches; also for branch-targeted PAUSE/RESUME/INVALIDATE). RESUME routing = RELEASE-IF-HELD-ELSE-FORWARD-UP: a node HOLDING the lock releases it LOCALLY and does NOT forward (normal pause/resume -- a controller targets the holder directly; a pull node holds its own pullId-lock); a node NOT holding it FORWARDS the RESUME up its deps (broadcast or the single towardDep edge) to find the holder. This makes a DEMAND (R-pull) a CONE-ROUTED RESUME of a pull node's pullId that travels up declared edges (inspectable, wave-ordered) WITHOUT the demander holding the target's reference; the pullId disambiguates which holder fires (siblings up one branch are told apart by pullId identity). PAUSE stays NODE-TARGETED (it ACQUIRES a lock, so there is no pre-existing holder to find -- a controller targets the node directly). DIRTY/INVALIDATE/TEARDOWN forward toward deps to the depless-source terminus (R-up-at-source). A forwarded RESUME whose lock NO node up the cone holds reaches the source terminus and is DROPPED (net no-op, R-pause-lockset / R-up-at-source). INTRA-graph only (D22).
rationale: D59. A demand must reach an upstream pull node WITHOUT a node reference (a reference IS the .cache anti-pattern: reach the node, read .cache) and WITHOUT an out-of-protocol side-channel; routing a RESUME up the DECLARED cone keeps the demand on inspectable, wave-ordered edges (describe/observe see it; .cache is an unordered invisible side-channel that bypasses wave ordering). 'release-if-held-else-forward-up' preserves normal pause/resume (the holder is targeted directly -> local release) while enabling cone-routed demand (a pull node pre-holds its pullId-lock from birth, so a routed RESUME always finds it); PAUSE needs no symmetric change (it creates a lock, no holder to find). Supersedes the old node-local-only RESUME: R-pause-lockset's 'RESUME of an unknown lock is a no-op' becomes 'forward up; drop at the terminus if unheld'. ctx.up(towardDep) prunes dead branches and is the general branch-targeted-control primitive.
